name: OpenAI Agents SDK for Python
tagline: A Python SDK for building agents with tools, handoffs, tracing, and realtime capabilities.
hook: A Python SDK guide to scope, released contracts, branch-local choices, visible-behavior tests, architecture, and compatibility.
summary: The Python Agents SDK guide puts firm limits on implementation and review scope. It distinguishes released contracts from choices made only on the current branch, asks tests to prove visible behavior, and maps runtime work to architecture references.

techniques.title: Define a concrete trigger for reconsidering complexity
techniques.body: Group related findings by root cause and reassess the full diff against the original requirement. This stops review fixes from accumulating compatibility branches without revisiting the design.
techniques.quote: A second related finding that adds another compatibility case or protocol hop triggers this reset.

techniques.title: Separate documentation need from release timing
techniques.body: Required documentation for behavior absent from the latest release belongs in separately timed work. The rule distinguishes missing content from content that would be inaccurate if published with the current feature PR.
techniques.quote: Determine whether documentation is required separately from deciding which pull request should carry it.

techniques.title: Treat public argument order as compatibility
techniques.body: The guide includes positional parameters and dataclass fields in the exported API contract. That makes seemingly additive changes subject to the behavior existing callers rely on.
techniques.quote: Treat the parameter and dataclass field order of exported runtime APIs as a compatibility contract.

techniques.title: Test the operation that survives a race
techniques.body: Concurrency evidence must control completion order and inspect surviving work and shared state. Merely running sequential happy paths cannot establish whether stale work overwrites a newer operation.
techniques.quote: For concurrency findings, require controlled completion ordering plus assertions about the surviving operation and final shared state.

techniques.title: Require an independent oracle for test expectations
techniques.body: Tests must exercise the stable caller-visible boundary that owns the outcome. Assertions that mirror helper calls or recompute expectations with implementation logic are explicitly insufficient.
techniques.quote: Do not accept helper-only call-shape assertions or expected values recomputed with the implementation's own logic when another layer owns the outcome.

techniques.title: Write source documentation for reliable translation
techniques.body: English source must state actors, ownership, ordering, and lifecycle explicitly while preserving API names and meaning. Ambiguity becomes a compatibility risk for generated translations.
techniques.quote: Treat translation-safe English as a documentation compatibility requirement.

steal: Give repeated scope expansion an explicit reset trigger.
Separate required documentation from its publication timing.
Include positional argument order in API compatibility checks.
Make race tests inspect surviving work and final shared state.
Derive expected behavior independently of implementation logic.
Write documentation with explicit actors and lifecycle subjects.
